# dsh-token-heatmap
中文 | English
A **daily token-usage heatmap** that adds a "Token usage" section to the DSH settings page. One cell
per day; theme-aware greyscale indicates relative usage.
Selecting a day also shows an **estimated cost in CNY**, derived from DeepSeek's published list pric
es and their peak/off-peak schedule.
All data is derived from DSH's own local session logs. **No external network requests and no separat
ed from DSH's own local session logs. **No external network requests and no separate usage ledger.**
> **Privacy**: this plugin makes no outbound requests. Session logs are read on the local machine on
ly, and the aggregated result is served to your local DSH page. The repository contains no personal
data or credentials.
## Design highlights
- **A native settings section, not an overlay.** The component registers into the `settings.section`
slot and renders React elements only. It does not append to `document.body`, does not replace the a
pplication root, and imports no Harness client package. It therefore occupies the settings sidebar a
longside the built-in sections rather than floating above the application. See Implementation notes.
- **Local data only, single source of truth.** No data leaves the machine and no additional ledger

is required: every figure is derived from the session logs DSH already writes.
- **The session log f
ormat is parsed explicitly.** Concatenated zstd frames, replayed `seq` values and truncated tail fra
mes are each handled as distinct cases. A single-pass decompression retains only the first frame of

a multi-frame log and therefore under-reports usage. See Data source.
- **Colour levels remain reada
ble at both ends of the scale.** The four metrics differ by orders of magnitude, so levels are deriv
ed from **quantiles of the local data set** (25th/50th/75th percentiles) rather than fixed threshold
s. Cache reads frequently account for the majority of a day — 99% in the screenshots below — which i

s why `Input+output` is provided as a separate metric.
- **Brightness is reserved for days with reco
rded usage.** Days without usage occupy the lowest visual level, so an otherwise empty grid remains
visually neutral and days with usage are distinguishable at a glance. This carries an accessibility

benefit as well: the encoding never relies on colour hue.
- **Cost is estimated rather than billed.*
* DSH session logs record token counts but no currency amounts, so the detail panel applies DeepSeek
's published CNY prices to the day's input, cache-read and output tokens. The peak/off-peak schedule
is accounted for per record using the record's own timestamp, and the panel states that the figure

is an estimate. See Cost estimate.
[该节后续省略]
## Screenshots
> **Note on screenshot currency.** The images below predate **v0.5.0** and have not been re-captured

since. Three UI changes made since are therefore not visible in them:
>
> 1. **Empty-day cells rend
er darker.** Days without recorded usage now occupy the dimmest level, reserving the brightness rang

e for days with usage (v0.4.1).
> 2. **Collapsing a day retains its selection.** Selecting the same
date again collapses only the detail body; the selection outline remains on the heatmap and the coll

apsed row carries an expand control (v0.4.1).
> 3. **The detail panel shows an estimated cost.** A d

aily cost in CNY is displayed next to the daily total (v0.5.0).
>
> The textual descriptions through
out this document reflect the current behaviour.
### Half-year heatmap and compact tooltip
Open Settings → **Token usage**. The default range is six months. Choose total, input+output, cache
read or output, and switch between daily and weekly views. The range selector offers six months or a
full year; the year is split into two rows.
Hover a date cell to display three lines: the date (YYYY-MM-DD), the selected metric's Token count,
and “Click to view details”. The example below shows 2026-10-13 with a total of 117,405,946 Token. S
electing the cell displays that day's breakdown below the heatmap. The outline indicates hover or se
lection; today's cell has no default highlight. Cells with no recorded usage remain at the dimmest l
evel, so the brightness range is reserved for days with usage.
## Features
- Default half-year range (26 weeks); full year uses two rows (27 + 26 weeks), each with month label

s
- Cells capped at 20px with 4px gaps, sized to the container to avoid horizontal scrollbars
- **Da
ily / Weekly** views: daily levels or one shared level per natural week; Sunday–Saturday, future dat

es empty
- **Four metrics**: total / input+output / cache read / output, rendered in theme-aware gra

yscale
- Hover or focus shows the cell's date, the selected metric's Token count and a click hint; w

eekly counts are labeled
- Click a date for inline daily details below the heatmap: total, input, ou
tput, cache reads, calls, nonzero cache writes, and an estimated cost in CNY; weekly cells open thei

r actual day
- Selecting the selected date again collapses the detail body while retaining its selec
tion outline; an expand control and `Esc` both collapse, and selecting another date switches without

an intermediate collapse
- **Cost estimate** based on DeepSeek's published CNY prices, including th
e peak/off-peak schedule applied per record timestamp; unknown models fall back to the Flash table a

nd are labelled as such. The English interface writes `CNY ¥4.98` so the currency is explicit.
- Pro

portional Token composition bar with percentages and an empty state
- Approximately 600ms diagonal e

ntrance without delaying the summary; filters and date selection do not replay it
- Native buttons s

upport Enter/Space and focus feedback; respects system reduced-motion preferences
- Today / this wee

k / all-time summary; minute refresh plus refresh on visibility or focus
- Chinese/English labels, m
onth names and number units; follows the host light/dark theme
